filename: Generative emulation of chaotic dynamics with coherent prior.pdf
title: Generative emulation of chaotic dynamics with coherent prior
venue: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering
testbed_rationale: Provides a reproducible benchmark combining turbulent fluid dynamics simulations and real-world subseasonal-to-seasonal atmospheric prediction datasets via ChaosBench, with open-source code and data.
pain_points: Long-range autoregressive skill decay and error accumulation leading to unphysical drift in chaotic dynamical systems
Blurring and oversmoothing from double penalty conundrum in deterministic deep learning weather prediction models over long lead times
Prohibitive computational expense of autoregressive diffusion models requiring iterative multi-step denoising at every timestep
High-dimensional neural operators suffer from severe numerical instability on long rollouts
Difficulty generating stable, physically consistent simulations from incomplete, noisy, or partially observed priors
extraction_notes: The paper interprets the generative denoising process of diffusion models as solving a Reynolds turbulence closure problem conditioned on a reduced-order model (deep Koopman operator or UNet++) coherent prior. Emulation is framed as single-pass trajectory planning across the entire horizon.
